Name: Lloyd R Bass
Question: What do you think of LeBron James calling himself the GOAT?
Answer: What do you think of LeBron James calling himself the GOAT? I think that Lebron has a relatively empty bag to back up his claims. Sure he’s had a great career, but so have many other players. Lebron has had some great underdog moments like beating the Warriors in 2016, but he’s had some epic chokes like losing to the Mavs in 2011. He’s put up the best career total points scored, but only led the NBA once in scoring and never won a champion while leading the league in scoring. Ultimately, I’m sure Lebron will be viewed as one of the All-Time great players in the NBA. But as of today, he’s farther from being the GOAT than the Denver Nuggets are from repeating as NBA champions. I know of only 1 player in NBA history who came onto a perennial lottery team that had never won a championship and took it from the gutter of the NBA to the franchise with the 3rd most championships in NBA history in 14 years while being retired for 1.8 of those years. In 2018, 20 years later, the Warrior tied them and passed them 4 years later in 2022. Still, 26 years later they stand only behind the Celtics, Lakers, and Warriors.

Question: If you have a high IQ, then I assume you’re very happy about it and rightfully so. What if one day you were told by multiple professionals that your IQ is barely low average. How upset would you be?
Answer: If you have a high IQ, then I assume you’re very happy about it and rightfully so. What if one day you were told by multiple professionals that your IQ is barely low average. How upset would you be? I don’t know that I would be upset, I would ask questions to see why they were saying this. This is not to say that I haven’t done some dumb things in my time. But it’s beyond stupid IMO to assume someone has a below-average IQ just because they do what you perceive to be dumb things. I’ve known some Mensa members who could do incredibly dumb things on a regular basis. From my experience, the situation you describe is usually caused by failure to talk through the issue. If you don’t understand why someone does what you consider “dumb” at the very least ask them why they do it instead of just assuming that they are stupid. Now if I asked and they would only tell me that they said it because “you are stupid”. Then, I’d rightly assume that they were the stupid party. They’d only upset me if they got in the way of me doing my job or made extra work for me because of their stupidity. However, if they responded with a description of a real problem, then I’d try and find a solution that would work for both of us if at all reasonable. I can still remember getting in trouble for finding errors in another team’s software bugs that had to interface with my team’s website. I’d always test their changes against a baseline before intergrating with the website instead of just trusting it was right. The alternative was to have the website break in production and waste our developement time developing to a broken standard that would take unplanned time to go back and fix. That upset me, because it got in the way of me doing the job I was hired to do.

Question: Who has scored more points in a regular season game, LeBron James or Michael Jordan?
Answer: Who has scored more points in a regular season game, LeBron James or Michael Jordan? Michael Jordan scored the most points in a single regular season game with 69. Lebron has a single game high of 61. Jordan also holds the all-time single game scoring record for a playoff game with 63.

Question: Do you think Michael Jordan would have won a championship without Scottie Pippen?
Answer: Do you think Michael Jordan would have won a championship without Scottie Pippen? I had to go and double check that this question wasn’t asked by Mars Blackmon because it uses similar logic that old Mars used to use. Yes, every major accomplishment as an NBA player that Michael Jordan made was wearing Air Jordans, but sorry Mars it wasn’t the shoes. Michael could still have accomplished all he did in the NBA using another brand of shoes. He most likely would be as rich from endorsements, but that’s not why most consider him the GOAT of basketball or that he won 10 scoring titles, 5 MVPs, 6 Final’s MVPS, etc. Likewise, every NBA championship that Michael Jordan won he had Scottie Pippen for a teammate. But it wasn’t because of Pippen that he won the championships. While Michael did need help to win each of his championships, that help could have come in many different forms. Scottie Pippen wasn’t needed, just some roughly equivalent talent would have sufficed. Take the last championship. Sub in Grant Hill or Tracy McGrady for Pippen, and I doubt it would have stopped MJ from getting his 6th championship.

Question: How can a convicted felon become successful? (so they won't have to go back down the road of crime)
Answer: It can be done with some luck and tons of hard work. However the criminal justice system including the often arbitrary and illogical terms of parole, probation, and other continuing state supervision lasting years, decades, or sometimes even for life; creates a barrier to convicted criminals to reintegrate into society as successful and contributing members of that society. This barrier can be overcome sometimes, but others will see a failure through no fault of the ex-criminal other than simply bad luck. An example of bad luck is that a clerk types in the wrong address for an ex-criminal, say 1213 acme street instead of 1312 acme drive. That means the ex-criminal doesn’t get a notice to appear, therefore fails to appear, and therefore is thrown back into jail or prison for violating the terms of their release. Others have the bad luck to get an jerk of a supervising officer which requires the ex-criminal to take 3 hours (1-hour commute each way and 1 hour waiting for and executing meeting) off work in the middle of the workweek to attend a mandatory supervised meeting. The downsides were excellently documented in the new PBS docuseries PHILLY D.A. | Films | PBS in episode 1.4 with the case of LaTonya Myers. The system desperately needs to be reformed from primarily focusing on punishment and making it difficult for ex-criminals to at least neutrality in reforming if not nurturing reformation. All this said there are some excellent people at all levels in the criminal justice system that go above and beyond what is required in successfully aiding many ex-criminals to successfully reintegrate into society and start a successful career path. Every situation has the potential to be vastly different because of the specific people involved.
